title: Checkpoint: Alexander and After
objective: After this level you can explain how Alexander spread Greek culture from Egypt to India.
summary: Alexander’s road ran from Chaeronea to the Hyphasis; after him, Greek cities like Ai Khanoum and the common Greek, Koine, spread Greek culture from Egypt to India.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: in Afghanistan, archaeologists found Greek advice from Delphi.
cards.body: How did Greek words end up so far from Greece? Follow Alexander’s road, then see what stayed behind.

events.label: Philip beats Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea
Gaugamela decides the war with Persia
The army refuses to go past the Hyphasis

cards.headline: A Greek city in Afghanistan
cards.body: At Ai Khanoum, in northern Afghanistan, stood a Greek city founded in the wake of Alexander’s conquests, complete with a gymnasium and a theater. There a man named Clearchus set up sayings copied from Delphi: ’As a child, be orderly; as a youth, self-controlled; as an adult, just; as an old man, of good counsel; when dying, without sorrow.’ Delphi’s advice, carved in Afghanistan.

cards.headline: The language that stayed
cards.body: Alexander’s soldiers went home. His language stayed. Koine, the common Greek of the Hellenistic age, was used from Greece and Macedonia to the Greek-ruled parts of Africa and the Middle East, and it lasted until the 6th century CE. The New Testament was written in it.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How Alexander's conquests spread Greek cities and the Greek language from Egypt to India.
How Philip's longer pikes and rebuilt army let Macedonia master the Greek cities.
Why Alexander's empire broke into rival kingdoms when he died without an adult heir.
Why Rome conquered Greece by force, yet ended up won over by Greek art and learning.

questions.prompt: What did Clearchus set up at Ai Khanoum, a Greek city in Afghanistan?

options.label: A statue of Bucephalus
options.rationale: It was an inscription of advice.

questions.explanation: Clearchus set up Delphic sayings, from ’as a child, be orderly’ to ’when dying, without sorrow’.

questions.prompt: Alexander and After recap: why did Greek outlast Alexander’s armies in the East?

options.label: Rome made Greek its only language
Persia’s kings adopted Greek before Alexander
Koine became the common language under Greek rulers
Every soldier stayed behind to teach it

questions.explanation: Koine Greek spread across the Greek-ruled East and lasted until the 6th century CE.

questions.prompt: Alexander and After recap: what gave Philip of Macedon’s soldiers their longer reach?

options.label: Elephants from India
options.rationale: Those came much later, with Seleucus.

questions.explanation: The sarissa was roughly twice as long as a Greek spear.

questions.prompt: On Alexander and After’s timeline, which event came right before Alexander’s death in Babylon?

options.label: Rome’s destruction of Corinth
options.rationale: That came much later, in 146 BCE.

options.label: The army’s refusal at the Hyphasis

questions.explanation: The army refused to go on at the Hyphasis in 326 BCE; Alexander died in 323 BCE.

questions.prompt: Alexander and After recap: which of the Successors’ kingdoms outlasted the others?

options.label: The Antigonids’ Macedonia
options.rationale: Rome ended it at Pydna in 168 BCE.

options.label: Porus’s kingdom in India
options.rationale: Porus ruled under Alexander, not as a Successor.

questions.explanation: Ptolemaic Egypt lasted until 30 BCE, longest of the three.
